title: Playing style, Davis brothers and jobs with heavy drinkers
summary: Lewis describes playing low register against the bands' style, mentions the Pierces and drummer Robert Davis, and recalls long jobs at Lushin's Place with fights and drinking.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: I try to play in one way, the bands play in another. I like to play low register. I'm trying to play Mario Blasch. There was a mic that beat this one. Those old men didn't know mic in those days. But we played whenever we were. I had to play low register. There's one thing a text we're going to be running out soon. I wanted to mention, if you could say something about, and this is this time when you were playing out of Bunky, just before Bill Russell came down here in 42. Could you just say something about that time when you were playing, who you were playing with, what the set up was? Well, the set up was Bill and the D. There was their job. Robert, the boy named Jim, Jimmy Davis' brother, Robert Davis, he was a drummer. Was the governor? Was Jimmy Davis the governor? When was the governor? No, Jimmy Davis the check and click. Jim, Jim, Jim did. I thought Jimmy Davis was the governor, but some kind of special kind of position. About stuff I know where Frank gives up. I think the footnote was Frank. Yes. He was on a tramway. What were you playing for? He was playing a little, when he found a nightclub. Every night? Every night, yeah. Except on Sundays. Except on Monday nights. We were all on Monday nights. And I played with Bill in the evening. I played with him a long time. I just got disgusted at home. At that time, the nice people now, they were always nice people. But they drank a little bit too much. I drank too. But when they was drinking, I drank it. And they would get on the room. There was many fights that they broke up at Lushin's Place. And they were just, I'm a little bit too. But I think it was the best thing that ever happened to them because they knew life now. See? I don't know.
